mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.5 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue growth expectations decline, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.3% from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.3% from prior month, or the Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing supply chain disruption (indicated by a decline in industrial production below 100 index level), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to elevated inflation and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% year-over-year signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% y/y, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) above 100,000 new jobs per month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by > 100,000 jobs, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (indicated by a GDP growth rate above 2.5% annualized), a decline in residential construction (HOUST) signals an impending slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized and HOUST declines, or the Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a supply shock coupled with labor market weakness, which reduces corporate profitability and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.
